Office of the Deputy Commissioner: Imphal East District (Deputy Commissioner Imphal East) has published the Recruitment 2026 notification for 3 vacancies, including Case Worker, Psycho-Social Counsellor, and Para Legal Personnel/Lawyer posts. The offline application process will be conducted from 20 November 2026 to 11 December 2026. For complete details, candidates can visit imphaleast.nic.in.

Office of the Deputy Commissioner: Imphal East District (Deputy Commissioner Imphal East), Manipur, has invited applications for 3 posts in 3 roles under Advt No. DC/(IE)/17/OSC/2019/1615. The posts include Case Worker, Psycho-Social Counsellor, Para Legal Personnel/Lawyer. Applications are to be sent offline and must reach the organisation by 11 December 2026.

The posts are for One Stop Centre (OSC-SAKHI), Imphal East District. Qualification required: Case Worker: woman with Bachelor in Law/Social Work/Sociology/Social Science/Psychology and at least 3 years' experience on women-related domains, resident of local community. Psycho-Social Counsellor: woman with professional degree/diploma in Psychology/Psychiatry/Neurosciences with health sector background. Para Legal Personnel/Lawyer: Degree in Law/legal training or knowledge of laws with 3 years' experience, or practising lawyer with 2 years' litigation experience. The pay is Rs. 14,600 per month (Pre-revised GP-2800) for each post. The application fee is Rs. 300 for Unreserved and OBC. Selection is by academic score, experience and personal interview/viva-voce. Post-wise eligibility, dates and the steps to apply are given below.

  • Last date: 11 December 2026
  • Vacancies: 3, in 3 roles
  • How to apply: Offline, by post or in person as the notification says

  • Full-time (Contractual); the position is purely temporary and contractual.

  • The Senior Consultant reports to the Project Coordinator and works closely with the research team at IIPA.

Essential Qualification

  • Master's degree in Environmental Science / Environmental Engineering / Water Resources / Civil Engineering, Natural Resources or related discipline from a recognised university.
  • And Ph.D. in any of the above-mentioned subjects.

Desirable Experience

  • Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in research, consultancy or project implementation in river basin planning, water quality assessment, sewage and septage management, solid waste management and river rejuvenation.
  • Prior work with NMCG/ CPCB/ SPCBs/ MoEF&CC/ CWC/ NWQMP/ NRCP/ CPHEEO or State Mission for Clean Ganga.
  • Demonstrated experience in GIS-based spatial analysis, pollution hotspot mapping and stakeholder consultations.
  • Research papers published in journals indexed in Scopus or Web of Science on water resources, pollution control or environmental governance.

Desirable Competencies

  • Understanding of Namami Gange programme, NGRBMP, NMCG guidelines and GIZ–IIPA District Ganga Planning Framework.
  • Strong knowledge of wastewater treatment, solid & plastic waste management, agricultural runoff control and nature-based solutions.
  • Proficiency in ArcGIS and QGIS for GIS-based spatial analysis and remote sensing.
  • Excellent analytical, report-writing and presentation skills.
  • Ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams and mentor junior researchers.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and statistical / analytical software (R, STATA, Python preferred).

Preferably below 50 years as of the closing date of the application. Relaxation may be considered in the case of exceptionally qualified and experienced candidates.

New Delhi, with travel to project districts in Uttar Pradesh (Hapur, Bulandshahr, Kasganj, Fatehpur, Kaushambi) and Bihar (Buxar, Bhojpur, Patna, Vaishali, Munger) and other locations as required for project-related activities.

  • Provide leadership, strategic and technical guidance for preparation of District Ganga Plans across ten districts.
  • Oversee baseline assessments, field investigations, pollution hotspot mapping and HVRCA studies.
  • Validate methodology, review draft plans, ensure quality assurance and alignment with NMCG guidelines.
  • Lead thematic action plans on wastewater, solid waste, agricultural runoff, wetland conservation and climate resilience.
  • Facilitate stakeholder consultations, capacity-building workshops and inter-departmental coordination.
  • Liaise with SMCG, District Administrations and District Ganga Committees.
  • Contribute to the final summary report with policy recommendations for scaling DGPs across the Ganga basin.
